title: Automated quantization onboarding and perf regression playbook (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create an automated onboarding playbook and CI pipeline for publishing quantization profiles (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) with integrated perf-regression detection and safe rollout gates. This ticket covers the end-to-end flow: profile generation, profile metadata schema, benchmark harness, automated regression checks, alerting, and documented rollback/pinning procedures. Deliverables: 1) quant-profile CI that ingests model artifacts and emits normalized profiles + performance metrics; 2) perf regression rules and thresholds stored with profile metadata; 3) runtime hooks to prefer pinned model+profile combos and auto-fallback to CPU/FP16 when regressions are detected; 4) console dashboard tiles and alerting for newly published profiles; 5) runbook for on-call and SRE containing rollback & pin steps.
acceptance_criteria: CI job produces a signed quantization profile JSON and stores it in the model catalog on success
Regression checks run in CI and compare new profile against baseline with token/sec, p50/p95 latency, and generation quality delta metrics
Profiles flagged as regressed fail the publish step and create a blocking incident ticket with artifacts (diff, flamegraphs, sample outputs)
Console displays profile version, quantization method, kernel hints, and recent perf trend for each model-version
Runtime respects explicit version pinning and falls back to a compatible FP16/FP32 variant when a profile is marked unhealthy
On-call runbook validated with a simulated bad profile and successful rollback within 30 minutes
technical_notes: Profile schema will include: quant_method (INT8|FP8|GPTQ|AWQ), calibration_seed, calibration_dataset_hash, kernel_hint, expected_mem_savings_pct, benchmark_inputs_hash, sample_outputs_hash, baseline_metrics_id. We will extend the existing perf harness (bench/quant-harness) to run 3 workload types: short-chat (<=128 tokens), long-context (>=2048 tokens), and embeddings/batched inference. Regression detection will use: p95 latency delta > 15% OR throughput regression > 20% OR quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) drop > configurable threshold. For GPTQ/AWQ we will also compare decoded sample logits on a small fixed prompt set to detect numerical instability. Signed profiles will be stored in S3 with immutability tags and catalog entry in model-registry service.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Build CI job and extended perf harness (2 weeks). Phase 2: Integrate regression checks, metadata storage, and publish gating (1 week). Phase 3: Runtime pinning support and fallback behavior (2 weeks). Phase 4: Console dashboard and alerting + runbook rehearsal (1 week). We'll run canary publishes to internal test orgs before allowing customer scope. Feature flags will gate automated publishes. Performance baselines will be selected from the most-recent validated profile; initial baselines seeded from last stable runtime-1.20 profiles.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Quantized profile passes microbenchmarks but causes subtle generation quality regressions in customer prompts. Mitigation: include a small curated prompt set from recent customer evals (anonymized) for quality checks and require a manual PM/ML signoff for first 3 major models. Risk: FP8/GPTQ numeric variance under different kernel implementations. Mitigation: record kernel_hint and require kernel compatibility checks in runtime; if kernel mismatch detected, runtime falls back to baseline variant.
rollout_strategy: 1) Internal: publish to 'internal-test' catalog and run for 7 days against synthetic + internal production traffic. 2) Partner: select 3 customers with non-critical workloads on dedicated capacity to opt into beta via account flag. 3) GA: enable publish for all hosted models with automated regression enforcement. Pinning: default behavior is to auto-assign profile but customer can set an explicit pin (model_version@profile_id). When a regression alert fires, the system automatically retags the profile as 'quarantined' and routes traffic to the pinned stable variant per account policy.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: profile publish success rate, average token/sec by quant_method, regression-failure rate, time-to-rollback. Alerts: publish-failure (SLA), regression-detected (pager), sudden-memory-increase (>30% vs baseline). Add an audit log entry for every publish and profile_state_change. Create a Grafana dashboard with linked traces and a developer-friendly 'investigate' link to the CI artifacts bucket.
